title: Exterior powers preserve module localization, characterized on pure wedges
statement: Let R and B be commutative rings, B an R-algebra which is a localization at a multiplicative submonoid S of R [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Let M be an R-module and N a B-module. Suppose f : M -> N is R-linear after restricting scalars and identifies N with the localization of M at S. Let n be a natural number and let g : exteriorPower_R^n M -> exteriorPower_B^n N be R-linear after restricting scalars [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. If g(m_1 wedge ... wedge m_n) = f(m_1) wedge ... wedge f(m_n) for every n-tuple of elements of M, then g identifies its codomain with the localization of its domain at S. This includes n=0, S containing zero, and modules without finiteness or freeness assumptions.

source.place: Proof step 2: localization of exterior powers by the pure-wedge fraction formula; based on Stacks Project, Algebra, Section 00DM and Schemes, Tags 01I8, 01IA and 01HV.

proof.text: Let L be LocalizedModule S (exteriorPower R n M), with localization map j. Equip L with the canonical B-module structure and scalar tower using IsLocalizedModule.module and isScalarTower_module. The action of every denominator on any B-module is invertible (isLocalizedModule_id).

Prove extension of R-multilinear maps M^n -> P, for any B-module P, by induction on n. In degree zero take the constant map. Curry the final variable, apply the induction hypothesis with codomain Hom_R(M,P), postcompose with IsLocalizedModule.map S f id, and uncurry. The map agrees on numerator tuples by map_apply and the induction hypothesis. Separately prove uniqueness: choose a common denominator t for a tuple in N^n; multilinearity multiplies both values by t^n, and multiplication by t^n is injective on P.

Apply multilinear extension to j composed with the universal wedge. Each coordinate R-linear map on N is B-linear by LinearMap.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization. To verify alternation, clear a common denominator of a tuple with equal coordinates i and j. Replace numerator i by numerator j; the images are unchanged, and the original alternating map vanishes on the modified numerator tuple. Cancel t^n to obtain vanishing on the localized tuple. The exterior universal property gives h : exteriorPower B n N -> L.

Extend g to k : L -> exteriorPower B n N by LocalizedModule.lift. Prove h k = id by localization extensionality and then exterior-power extensionality on numerator wedges, using hg and the extension formula. Extend k to a B-linear map. Prove k h = id by exterior-power extensionality, the multilinear uniqueness lemma from step 2, and the same calculation on numerator tuples. The resulting R-linear equivalence identifies g with its composite with j, so IsLocalizedModule.of_linearEquiv proves the claim. Degree zero and a submonoid containing zero are included throughout: no positive-degree or nonzero-denominator assumption is made.

mathlib_searches.results: No exterior-power localization declaration. CliffordAlgebra.equivBaseChange concerns the entire algebra, not its individual exterior powers. Blueprint exterior search and DAG statement search found no duplicate algebraic localization node.

lean.statement:
theorem isLocalizedModule_of_wedge
    {R B : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    (S : Submonoid R) [IsLocalization S B]
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) (N : ModuleCat.{u} B)
    (f : M ⟶ (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R B)).obj N)
    [IsLocalizedModule S f.hom] (n : ℕ)
    (g : ModuleCat.of R (⋀[R]^n M) ⟶
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R B)).obj (ModuleCat.of B (⋀[B]^n N)))
    (hg : ∀ a : Fin n → M,
      g (ιMulti R n a) = ιMulti B n (fun i ↦ f (a i))) :
    IsLocalizedModule S g.hom
